subject: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint
messages:
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint

Hi Elena —

Thanks for taking the call earlier. As we prepare the private endpoint pack for ProspectCorp's on‑prem runtime, we want to confirm the exact egress controls you require so our ops handoff and evidence package match your security gate. High level asks below — please confirm or correct: 

1) FQDN allowlist: you require exact hostnames (no wildcard *.redwood.com entries) and SNI validation must be preserved.
2) TLS: outbound must allow TLS 1.3 (no TLS interception/mitm by upstream proxies). If you require TLS inspection, we need the intercept certs/fingerprint process documented.
3) Ports: only TCP/443 outbound to the listed FQDNs; DNS resolution should go to your resolver (UDP/TCP 53) unless otherwise stated.
4) IP provenance: Redwood will provide a small ephemeral NAT pool; you want a signed attest that lists the pool, rotation window, and the operator contact.
5) Telemetry headers: Redwood will emit X-Redwood-Request-Id and X-Redwood-Region headers on outbound connections for tracing. Is adding these headers acceptable? If not, what is your preferred correlation mechanism?

Can you attach the latest internal allowlist template (hostnames + required cert SANs) and confirm whether you need per‑request mTLS (client cert) or just server-side validation? Once we have confirmation, we’ll produce the evidence bundle (IP manifest, packet-snippet examples, and a short test harness) for your SOC intake.

Thanks — David

--
David Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-01T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint

David —

Thanks, that summary is close. A few specifics from our side: 

- FQDN allowlist: correct, exact hostnames only. We do not accept wildcard entries. Provide hostnames and expected certificate SANs.
- SNI/TLS: ProspectCorp maintains strict TLS 1.3 end‑to‑end. No interception allowed. If your runtime requires upstream proxying that tampers with TLS, we will need a detailed design and a compensating control.
- Ports: TCP/443 only. We allow TCP/853 for DNS over TLS in exceptional cases (must be pre-approved). Otherwise DNS must point to our resolver IPs.
- NAT pool: we prefer a short static range (up to 10 IPs) that can be rotated quarterly. Each rotation must be accompanied by the new IP manifest and an operational window (UTC times) so our firewall team can stage the change.
- Telemetry headers: Acceptable but must not expose PII. X-Redwood-Request-Id and X-Redwood-Region are fine. If you send X-User-Id or any end-user identifier, that will be rejected.

Attachments: I’ve attached ProspectCorp_allowlist_template.xlsx with the hostname column and cert_fingerprint column. Also attaching ProspectCorp_Egress_SLA_v1.pdf — contains our rotation approval SLA and change window template.

Regards,
Elena

--
Elena Gomez
Security Engineer, ProspectCorp
elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com
[attachment: ProspectCorp_allowlist_template.xlsx (xlsx)]
[attachment: ProspectCorp_Egress_SLA_v1.pdf (pdf)]

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T08:13:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint

Elena —

Appreciate the quick response and the attached templates — got them. Two clarifying questions before we assemble the evidence bundle: 

1) IP binding model: can we submit a primary static NAT pool of up to 8 IPs plus an ephemeral overflow pool of 16 IPs that are advertised only during high-burst windows? The primary pool will be the one you allow in the production firewall; ephemeral overflow will require a separate scheduled approval per your SLA.

2) Telemetry header constraints: we will not send any end-user identifiers. We plan to include X-Redwood-Request-Id (UUID v4), X-Redwood-Region, and an X-Redwood-Eval-Flag (true/false) used for internal routing/quality tracing. Is X-Redwood-Eval-Flag OK if it contains only boolean values?

If both are OK we’ll produce: 
- IP manifest (CSV) with ASN, hex fingerprints, and primary/overflow classification
- Sample pcap + curl example showing SNI preserved and headers present
- Short runbook for rotating the primary NAT pool (with UTC windows)

Targeting a first draft evidence bundle by 2028-04-03 EOD.

Best,
David

--
David Kim
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com>, David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint

Hi Elena —

Quick operational note from the Dedicated Ops side: if you accept the primary/overflow model David proposed, please confirm these constraints so our network team engineers the NAT translation correctly: 

- Primary NAT pool (static): 8 IPv4 addresses; will be advertised from day 1.
- Overflow pool (ephemeral): up to 16 IPv4 addresses that we only advertise during scheduled bursts; each rotation or advertisement event will be accompanied by the IP manifest and a 2‑hour scheduled cutover window.
- TTL and keepalive: TCP sessions preserve source IP for 90s after idle to avoid mid-stream NAT flips; we can shorten to 30s on request.
- Firewall rule suggestions: outbound to allowed FQDNs, port 443; DNS only to ProspectCorp resolvers. We will send an exemplar iptables/nftables snippet in the evidence bundle.

Also attaching a small CSV (redwood-egress-header-spec.csv) that documents the header names, value format, and examples. We will not include any PII.

Kimberly

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: redwood-egress-header-spec.csv (csv)]

From: Elena Gomez <elena.gomez@prospectcorp.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Liu <aaron.liu@prospectcorp.com>
Date: 2028-04-03T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FQDN outbound verification, telemetry headers, and allowlist constraints for private endpoint

David/Kimberly —

Thanks — we’re good to proceed with the primary (8 IPs) + overflow (up to 16 IPs) model. Please ensure the evidence bundle includes: 

- Signed IP manifest (CSV) with a PGP signature or equivalent attestation.
- Sample TLS handshake traces showing SNI preserved when X-Redwood headers are present.
- A small test harness (curl + headers) and an iptables snippet we can drop into our lab firewall for validation.
- Change window template filled out for the first rotation (propose 2028-07-01T02:00:00Z, 2-hour window).

We received ProspectCorp_allowlist_template.xlsx and ProspectCorp_Egress_SLA_v1.pdf — will begin internal review. We’ll flag any concerns by 2028-04-06.

Closing note: do not include any user identifiers in outbound headers; boolean flags and UUIDs are acceptable.

Elena

--
Elena Gomez
Security Engineer, ProspectCorp
